title: Soft-fence home-region affinity with burst-capacity escrow and graded circuit-breakers
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: During recent cross-region incidents we saw two failure modes: (1) aggressive geo-hedging pushed steady traffic away from a customer's home region for prolonged periods, increasing p95 latency and failing local compliance needs; (2) binary circuit-breakers tripped wholesale and caused large percent of traffic to failover without graceful degradation. Proposal: implement a 'soft-fence' home-region affinity policy combined with a per-region burst-capacity escrow and graded (proportional) circuit-breakers. Goal is to keep most traffic local when safe, allow controlled short bursts out-of-region during transient congestion, and step down capacity gracefully rather than total cutover. This integrates with existing latency-based routing, KV-cache locality heuristics, and capacity hint signals.
acceptance_criteria: Policy enforces home-region affinity for >= 90% of requests under normal load
Burst-escrow mechanism allows up to X tokens (configurable) per region and decays over Y seconds
Graded circuit-breaker reduces routed traffic to degraded paths incrementally (10%, 30%, 60%) rather than fully tripping
Integrated telemetry emitted (home_affinity_ratio, escrow_tokens_used, cb_level, reroute_latency_p95) and visible in Console dashboard
Canary rollout shows no >2% error increase and no SLO p95 breaches >5 minutes during controlled stress tests
design_decisions: Affinity model: soft-fence with hysteresis — prefer home region when p95 < latency_threshold and capacity_credits > min_credit
Escrow: allocate per-region burst credits that accrue at steady low-rate and can be consumed for short hedging; credits decay after 60s to limit long-term drift
Circuit-breaker: implement 3-level proportional breaker (level 1: -10% reroute, level 2: -30%, level 3: -60%) determined by combined signals from capacity_utilization and rising latency percentiles
Decision to prioritize KV-cache hit preservation when choosing fallback region — fallback scoring adds +20% weight for cache locality
Failure modes: if escrow depleted and CB at level 3, fall back to SLA-tier-aware shedding (non-critical low-tier requests are shed first)
Operator controls: expose escrow window, CB thresholds, and hysteresis time constants in Console with per-customer override capability for Dedicated/Private
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): unit tests and local simulation validating escrow accounting and CB transitions
Stage 1 (canary): 1% of traffic globally, observe metrics for 48h, run synthetic stress scenarios (spiky requests and sustained load)
Stage 2 (gradual): 10% -> 30% over 72h contingent on no regressions
Stage 3 (opt-in): enable for subset of customers in staged config with ability to toggle per-org
Rollback: revert routing flag and disable escrow consumption if p95 errors >2% above baseline for >15m
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for home-region vs fallback-region
error_rate and availability per region and overall
test_plan: Unit tests for escrow arithmetic, decay window, and edge cases (wrap, negative balance)
Integration tests: simulate mixed traffic across three regions with scripted capacity drops and ensure graded CB behaves as expected
Chaos run: throttle one region for 10s bursts and validate that home_affinity_ratio decays gracefully and then recovers
Load test: gradual increase to 150% baseline to ensure proportional reroute limits and that KV-locality heuristics keep cache hit delta <5%
Security test: ensure per-customer override respects RBAC and audit logs are emitted
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboard tile: routing/soft_fence_summary with home_affinity_ratio and escrow usage
Alerts: escrow_consumption_rate > 50% sustained for 10m -> paging to SRE; cb_level == 3 and p95_home_region > SLO -> high severity
SLO detection: automated alert when p95 tail breaches 2x configured SLO for >10m
Tracing: add tag route_policy=soft_fence and cb_level on request spans
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: escrow may be gamed by bursty tenants — mitigation: per-org cap and cooldown windows
Risk: complexity increases debugging when multiple policies interact — mitigation: enrich debug logs and add a routing-simulator tool in repo
Risk: fallback region overload — mitigation: integrate with autoscaler hints and prefer lower-cost reroutes when capacity low
Risk: KV cache locality loss increases token cost — mitigation: penalty weight in fallback scoring and preferential routing to regions with high cache hit probability
